# official-runtime-setup-guide (reference summary)

## Purpose
Establish official runtime prerequisites and setup boundaries before any Blender execution claim.

Establish runtime setup prerequisites, per-path minimum versions, source-confidence labels, truth-state defaults, and single-bridge boundaries before any Blender execution claim.

## Metadata & truth boundary
- **Canonical skill:** `skills/official-runtime-setup-guide/SKILL.md`
- **Contract:** `skills/official-runtime-setup-guide/contract.json` (`v1.0.0`)
- **Category / role:** `runtime-and-execution` / `path-1-and-2-setup-instructor`
- **Capability tier:** `L0`
- **Truth-state policy:** Runtime status defaults to `Not Run`; Artifact status defaults to `Not Produced`; mutation rule is `downgrade_only` (never upgrade without verified evidence).

## When to use
- beginning of a Blender-related task before any runtime path is executed
- user asks what prerequisites, version floors, or setup boundaries apply
- framing official vs third-party vs CLI appendix constraints before handoff

## Trigger cues
- "set up Blender runtime prerequisites"
- "what are the Blender runtime setup boundaries"
- "prepare Official Blender Lab MCP setup prerequisites"
- "runtime prerequisites and version minimums"

## When not to use
- to install or configure a runtime automatically → delegate to `runtime-path-picker` (`references/skills/runtime-path-picker.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to runtime-path-picker)
- to claim runtime execution has already succeeded → delegate to `path-one-host-outline` (`references/skills/path-one-host-outline.md`; Delegates out-of-scope requests to path-one-host-outline)
- to choose a runtime path → delegate to `official-runtime-readiness-checker` (`references/skills/official-runtime-readiness-checker.md`; official-runtime-readiness-checker)

## Inputs & output/evidence contract
### Required inputs
- `selected_runtime_path` (`string`): Chosen execution path from runtime-path-picker (Path 1 Lab MCP, Path 2 mcp-for-blender, or CLI appendix)
- `host_client_environment` (`string`): User MCP host application (Claude Desktop Connector, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, or manual client)

### Optional inputs
- `installed_blender_version` (`string`): Installed Blender version used to check the Blender 5.1+ floor for Path 1 vs 3.0+ for Path 2

### Primary outputs
- `step_by_step_setup_prerequisites`
- `path_version_and_host_boundary_notes`
- `readiness_verification_handoff`

## Quick-start procedure
1. confirm this skill fits your goal
2. provide required inputs first
3. keep runtime claims evidence-bound

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- **Runtime boundary:** - This skill does not install or configure Blender runtime. - This skill does not run Blender or emit Python. - This skill does not provide custom CLI/MCP/addon runtime. - This skill frames **two MCP execution paths plus a CLI fallback appendix** (see `docs/runtime-stack-strategy.md`): - **Path 1 — Official Blender Lab MCP** (in Blender 5.1+, add-on manifest literal `blender_version_min = "5.1.0"`, hosted from either (a) Anthropic Connector in Claude Desktop OR (b) any manually configured MCP client). The Anthropic Connector is **not** standalone — Anthropic's tutorial step 2 installs the Lab add-on inside Blender; although the tutorial prerequisite says "Blender 4.2 or later", the binding floor is **Blender 5.1+**. Sources: https://claude.com/resources/tutorials/using-the-blender-connector-in-claude (host a), https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/ (Blender side, both hosts). - **Path 2 — Community `mcp-for-blender` (renamed from `ahujasid/blender-mcp`)** (third-party, minimum **Blender 3.0+**, exposes nine tools including `get_scene_info` and `execute_blender_code`). Use **only with caveats** and **never as release evidence**. Source: https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender - **CLI fallback (appendix only)** — direct `blender --background --python`, **never a peer path without an eval record**. Documented flags: `--background`, `--python`, `-E/--engine` (run `blender -E help` for exact engine tokens; Eevee token is `BLENDER_EEVEE` on 4.0–4.1 and 5.x, `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT` on 4.2–4.x). Source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/advanced/command_line/index.html
